A) Chip EDA ends at the package; board EDA designs the transistors

B) Board EDA interconnects off-the-shelf packages on a few to a few dozen layers; chip EDA creates the devices and wiring on the die

C) Board EDA and chip EDA use the same standard-cell placer and differ only in units

D) Board EDA has no design rules because fabrication is cheap
sample.answer: Board EDA interconnects off-the-shelf packages on a few to a few dozen layers; chip EDA creates the devices and wiring on the die
sample.explanation: The board flow starts where the chip flow ends: the die is already packaged, and the board tool wires packages together and models the board's own interconnect.

concepts.label: Symbols, footprints and land patterns
concepts.definition: Every board part exists in two views. The schematic symbol is logical: pins with names, numbers and electrical types.

sample.question:
In IPC terms, what is the land pattern of a component?

A) The schematic symbol of the part

B) The copper pad geometry on the board that the component's terminations solder to

C) The silkscreen outline drawn around the part

D) The paste stencil aperture only
sample.answer: The copper pad geometry on the board that the component's terminations solder to
sample.explanation: A land is a pad; the land pattern is the set of pads for one package. The footprint adds mask, paste, silkscreen, courtyard and assembly data around it.

concepts.label: Bills of materials
concepts.definition: The bill of materials (BOM) lists what must be bought and placed to build one board: one line per manufacturer part number, with its quantity, reference designators and approved sources.

sample.question: A schematic contains these placements: C1: 4.7 uF 0805 X5R capacitor; Y1: 12 MHz 3225 crystal; U1: SOT-23-5 LDO regulator; R1: 10 kohm 0603 resistor; C2: 4.7 uF 0805 X5R capacitor; U2: QFN-48 microcontroller; R2: 1 kohm 0402 resistor; U3: SOT-23-5 LDO regulator. The BOM has one line per manufacturer part number, and each distinct value-and-package description above is one part number. How many lines does the BOM have?
sample.explanation: Group the 8 placements by description. Same value in a different package is a different part number, so it gets its own line. There are 6 distinct descriptions.

concepts.label: Netlist handoff and annotation
concepts.definition: The netlist is the contract between schematic capture and layout. It lists each net as a set of pins, written as reference designator and pin number, and binds each designator to a footprint.

sample.question:
What does annotation do in schematic capture?

A) Assigns a unique reference designator such as R12 or U3 to every component

B) Generates a footprint for each symbol

C) Assigns net names to every pin

D) Adds explanatory notes to the printed schematic
sample.answer: Assigns a unique reference designator such as R12 or U3 to every component
sample.explanation: Reference designators are the keys that join schematic, netlist, BOM, layout and assembly data.

concepts.label: Electrical rule checking of schematics
concepts.definition: Electrical rule checking (ERC) runs on the schematic before layout. It reads each net's pins and their declared electrical types and flags combinations that cannot work: two outputs fighting, an input that nothing drives, a power input with no source, a net with a single pin.
key_ideas: Pin types and the conflict matrix
Evaluating the rules net by net

sample.question: An ERC flags a net if (a) the net has only one pin, or (b) it has two or more pins of type output or power output. The nets are: N1: U1 pin 16 (output), U4 pin 18 (output); N2: U3 pin 24 (output); N3: U3 pin 5 (passive), U5 pin 18 (output), U2 pin 2 (output); N4: U4 pin 5 (passive). How many nets does the ERC flag?
sample.explanation: Test every net against each rule and count a net once even if it breaks two rules. Flagged: N1, N2, N3, N4.

concepts.label: The PCB tool landscape
concepts.definition: Board design tools range from open-source suites to enterprise platforms. For a tool designer the useful questions are not which buttons they have, but what data model each exposes, how open its file formats and scripting are, how it represents constraints, and how designs move between tools.

sample.question:
A team wants to run a custom board check over hundreds of designs with an open toolchain. Which KiCad property helps most?

A) Output limited to Gerber files

B) Cloud-only design storage

C) An encrypted binary database

D) Readable text board files plus a Python scripting interface
sample.answer: Readable text board files plus a Python scripting interface
sample.explanation: Text files can be parsed, diffed and version-controlled, and scripting exposes the board model to custom checks.

concepts.label: Stackup build: thickness, layer count and symmetry
concepts.definition: A stackup is the ordered list of copper layers and dielectrics that make up the board: cores, prepregs, copper weights and the finished thickness.

sample.question: A 6-layer stackup from top to bottom is: L1 copper 1 oz, dielectric 14.5 mil, L2 copper 1 oz, dielectric 4.5 mil, L3 copper 1 oz, dielectric 7.5 mil, L4 copper 0.5 oz, dielectric 16.5 mil, L5 copper 1 oz, dielectric 15 mil, L6 copper 2 oz. Take 1 oz copper as 1.37 mil thick and ignore solder mask. What is the finished board thickness, in mil? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: Dielectrics sum to 58 mil. Copper totals 6.5 oz, which is 6.5 x 1.37 = 8.91 mil. The board is 66.91 mil thick.

concepts.label: Trace resistance from copper weight
concepts.definition: A trace is a resistor of rectangular cross-section. Its resistance sets the DC voltage drop on power traces, the loss at low frequency, and the self-heating that limits current.

sample.question: A trace is 200 mm long and 0.5 mm wide in 0.5 oz copper. Use $\rho = 1.72 \times 10^{-8}\ \Omega\cdot$m and take 1 oz copper as 35 micrometres thick, so $R = \rho L / (w t)$. What is its resistance, in milliohms? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: Thickness is 17.5 micrometres. $R = 1.72 \times 10^{-8} \cdot 0.2 / (0.0005 \cdot 0.0000175) = 393.1$ milliohms, with every length in metres.

concepts.label: Trace current capacity rules of thumb
concepts.definition: How wide must a trace be to carry a given current? The trace heats from $I^2 R$ loss and cools through the laminate and the air, so the answer is a temperature-rise limit, not a hard current limit.

sample.question: Use the IPC-2221 rule of thumb $I = k\, \Delta T^{0.44} A^{0.725}$, with $I$ in amperes, temperature rise $\Delta T$ in C, cross-section $A$ in square mils, $k = 0.048$ for outer layers and $k = 0.024$ for inner layers, and 1 oz copper 1.37 mil thick. An outer-layer trace is 50 mil wide in 0.5 oz copper. What current gives a 10 C rise? Answer in amperes, rounded to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Stackups and controlled impedance
concepts.definition: A fast edge on a board trace travels as a wave on a transmission line made of the trace and its reference plane.

sample.question: Use the IPC-2141 microstrip approximation $Z_0 = \frac{87}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r + 1.41}} \ln\frac{5.98 h}{0.8 w + t}$, where $h$ is the dielectric height to the plane, $w$ the trace width and $t$ the copper thickness. A surface trace has $w = 9.8$ mil, $t = 2.1$ mil, $h = 6.5$ mil and $\varepsilon_r = 4.6$. What is $Z_0$, in ohms? Round to 1 decimal place.

concepts.label: Propagation delay and effective dielectric constant
concepts.definition: A signal on a board trace moves at the speed of light divided by the square root of the effective dielectric constant the field sees.

sample.question: Light travels 11.8 inches per nanosecond in vacuum, so a line's delay is $t_{pd} = \sqrt{\varepsilon_{eff}} / 11.8$ ns per inch. A stripline is fully embedded in a dielectric with $\varepsilon_r = 3$, so $\varepsilon_{eff} = \varepsilon_r$. What is its delay, in ps per inch? Round to 1 decimal place.

concepts.label: Flex and rigid-flex boards
concepts.definition: Flexible circuits put copper on thin polyimide film so the board can bend, either once at installation or repeatedly in service.
key_ideas: Routing and features in flex regions

sample.question:
In a rigid-flex board, what forms the flexible region?

A) Flexible polyimide layers that run out of the rigid sections with no rigid material laminated over them

B) A cable soldered between two rigid boards

C) FR-4 milled down to a thinner section

D) Copper wires molded into silicone
sample.answer: Flexible polyimide layers that run out of the rigid sections with no rigid material laminated over them
sample.explanation: The flex layers are continuous through the rigid sections, where they are laminated with rigid material, and left bare between them.

concepts.label: Via types
concepts.definition: A via is a plated hole that connects copper on different layers. Its type is defined by which layers it spans and how it is made: through vias span the whole board, blind vias start at an outer layer and stop inside, buried vias join only inner layers, and microvias are small laser-drilled blind structures spanning one dielectric.

sample.question:
Which via joins an outer layer to an inner layer without passing through the whole board?

A) A thermal via

B) A blind via

C) A buried via

D) A through via
sample.answer: A blind via
sample.explanation: A blind via is visible on one surface only and ends at an inner layer.

concepts.label: Via aspect ratios and drill limits
concepts.definition: The aspect ratio of a plated hole is its depth divided by its drilled diameter. It limits how well plating solution reaches the middle of the barrel, so fabricators cap it, and the cap ties the board thickness to the smallest through via.
key_ideas: Minimum drill from a fab limit

sample.question: A 93 mil thick board has through vias drilled at 10 mil. The aspect ratio is board thickness divided by drilled hole diameter, written $x$:1. What is $x$? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $93 / 10 = 9.3$. High ratios make it hard for plating solution to reach the middle of the barrel, so the copper there thins.

concepts.label: HDI build-ups and microvia stacking
concepts.definition: High-density interconnect (HDI) boards add thin build-up layers to a conventional core, connected by laser-drilled microvias, so fine-pitch BGAs can escape without through vias.
key_ideas: The i plus N plus i notation

sample.question: HDI build-ups are written $i + N + i$: an $N$-layer core with $i$ sequential build-up layers on each side. A 12-layer board uses 3 build-up layers on each side. How many layers does its core have?
sample.explanation: $12 - 2 \cdot 3 = 6$ core layers, so the board is 3+6+3.

concepts.label: Board placement and ratsnest length
concepts.definition: Board placement positions a few hundred to a few thousand heterogeneous packages under mechanical, thermal, electrical and assembly constraints.
key_ideas: Ratsnest as a minimum spanning tree

sample.question:
Where should a decoupling capacitor be placed?

A) Next to the voltage regulator only

B) Near the board edge to save space

C) As close as possible to the power pin it serves, with a short low-inductance path to its vias and plane

D) Anywhere on the net, since the plane is ideal
sample.answer: As close as possible to the power pin it serves, with a short low-inductance path to its vias and plane
sample.explanation: The capacitor's benefit at high frequency is limited by the loop inductance of its connection, which grows with distance.

concepts.label: Board autorouters versus chip routers
concepts.definition: Board and chip routers share algorithms (maze search, rip-up and reroute, negotiated congestion) but face different problems.

sample.question:
Which early step dominates routing a large BGA board?

A) Choosing the copper weight

B) Fanout and escape: bringing every ball out to a via and a routing channel

C) Drilling the mounting holes

D) Placing the silkscreen
sample.answer: Fanout and escape: bringing every ball out to a via and a routing channel
sample.explanation: Escape determines how many layers the board needs. Once the balls are out, the remaining routing is comparatively open.

concepts.label: BGA fanout and escape routing
concepts.definition: A ball grid array puts hundreds or thousands of connections under one package. Escape routing brings each ball out from under the package to a routing channel, through traces between balls and vias down to other layers.
key_ideas: Counting balls in the outer rows

sample.question: A BGA has a 650 micrometre ball pitch and 300 micrometre pads. Traces are 75 micrometres wide with 125 micrometre clearance to pads and to each other. $N$ traces fit between two adjacent pads when $N w + (N + 1) s \le p - d$. How many traces fit between adjacent pads?

concepts.label: Odd and even modes of coupled lines
concepts.definition: Two traces routed side by side over a plane are coupled: each has mutual capacitance and mutual inductance to the other.
key_ideas: Two modes of a coupled pair

sample.question:
Two traces of a pair are brought closer together. What happens to the even-mode impedance?

A) It becomes infinite

B) It rises above the impedance of one uncoupled trace

C) It stays equal to the uncoupled impedance

D) It falls below the uncoupled impedance
sample.answer: It rises above the impedance of one uncoupled trace
sample.explanation: In the even mode both lines swing together, so the mutual capacitance carries no charge and the mutual inductance adds to each line's inductance.

concepts.label: Differential pairs
concepts.definition: A differential pair carries one signal as the voltage difference between two traces.
key_ideas: From odd mode to differential impedance

sample.question: A field solver reports an edge-coupled pair with odd-mode impedance 41.7 ohms and even-mode impedance 62.7 ohms. What is the differential impedance, in ohms? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: $Z_{diff} = 2 Z_{odd} = 2 \cdot 41.7 = 83.4$ ohms. The even-mode value does not enter.

concepts.label: Length matching from a skew budget
concepts.definition: Signals that must arrive together, the two traces of a differential pair or the data lines of a memory byte lane and their strobe, are given a skew budget in picoseconds.
key_ideas: Matching a group to a strobe

sample.question: The two traces of a differential pair differ in length by 95 mil, and the layer's delay is 175 ps per inch. What is the intra-pair skew, in ps? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: 95 mil is 0.095 in, times 175 ps per inch is 16.62 ps. Skew converts part of the differential signal into common mode.

concepts.label: Reflections at board impedance discontinuities
concepts.definition: When a wave on a board trace meets a change of impedance, at a load, a via, a connector or a width change, part of it reflects.
key_ideas: Launch voltage and the first arrival

sample.question: A 85 ohm trace ends in a 100 ohm load. The reflection coefficient is $\Gamma = (Z_L - Z_0)/(Z_L + Z_0)$. What is $\Gamma$? Round to 3 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $\Gamma = (100 - 85)/(100 + 85) = 0.081$. A load above $Z_0$ reflects a same-sign wave; a load below it reflects an inverted one.

concepts.label: IBIS models
concepts.definition: IBIS (I/O Buffer Information Specification) is the standard behavioral model of a chip's I/O buffers for board-level signal integrity.
key_ideas: Reading drive strength from a V-I table
Corners, power and the limits of IBIS

sample.question:
Why do silicon vendors publish IBIS models instead of SPICE netlists?

A) IBIS is more accurate than SPICE in every case

B) SPICE cannot model I/O buffers

C) IBIS hides the transistor design and simulates much faster while still predicting the waveform at the pin

D) IBIS contains the layout database
sample.answer: IBIS hides the transistor design and simulates much faster while still predicting the waveform at the pin
sample.explanation: Behavioral tables protect IP and make board-level simulation of many nets practical.

concepts.label: Touchstone files and channel S-parameters
concepts.definition: Passive board structures at high frequency, such as traces, vias, connectors and packages, are described by scattering parameters measured or simulated over frequency.

sample.question: A Touchstone file named channel.s12p holds the data of a 12-port network. How many complex S-parameters does it store at each frequency point?
sample.explanation: An $N$-port network has an $N \times N$ scattering matrix: $12^2 = 144$ entries per frequency.

concepts.label: IBIS-AMI and SerDes channel simulation
concepts.definition: Multi-gigabit serial links depend on equalization: transmit FFE, receive CTLE and DFE, and clock-data recovery.

sample.question:
In a statistical, Init-only AMI flow, what does the model process?

A) The bill of materials

B) The board's Gerber files

C) A long bit-by-bit waveform with adaptation

D) The channel impulse response, returning an equalized impulse response, under a linear time-invariant assumption
sample.answer: The channel impulse response, returning an equalized impulse response, under a linear time-invariant assumption
sample.explanation: If the equalizer is linear and fixed, its effect on the impulse response is enough to build an eye and BER statistically.

concepts.label: Power delivery: target impedance and decoupling
concepts.definition: A power delivery network (PDN) carries current from the regulator through planes, capacitors, package and die to every transistor.
key_ideas: Counting capacitors for an inductive limit

sample.question: A 1.8 V rail may ripple by at most 3% while its load current steps by 34 A. The PDN target impedance is $Z_t = V \cdot \text{ripple} / \Delta I$. What is $Z_t$, in milliohms? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $1.8 \cdot 0.03 / 34 = 1.59$ milliohms. The PDN must stay below this from DC up to the frequency where the package and die take over.

concepts.label: Through-hole versus surface-mount technology
concepts.definition: Components attach to a board in two ways. Through-hole technology (THT) passes leads through plated holes and solders them, usually by wave or selective soldering.
key_ideas: Two ways to attach a part

sample.question:
How is a surface-mount component attached to a board?

A) Its leads are crimped to the traces

B) Its terminations sit on surface lands printed with solder paste and are joined in a reflow oven

C) Its leads pass through plated holes and are wave soldered

D) It is clipped into a socket
sample.answer: Its terminations sit on surface lands printed with solder paste and are joined in a reflow oven
sample.explanation: SMT prints paste through a stencil, places parts on the wet paste and melts it in a controlled oven profile.

concepts.label: Design for assembly
concepts.definition: Design for assembly (DFA) is the set of layout rules that make a board cheap and reliable to build: fiducials and handling edges for the machines, spacing and orientation for placement and inspection, thermal and via rules for good joints, and BOM and side choices that cut setups.

sample.question:
Why do through-hole pads on planes use thermal reliefs?

A) To raise its current capacity

B) To lower the pad's impedance

C) Spokes limit heat flow into the plane so the joint can reach soldering temperature

D) To keep solder mask off the pad
sample.answer: Spokes limit heat flow into the plane so the joint can reach soldering temperature
sample.explanation: A solid connection to a large plane sinks heat, giving cold joints and hard rework.

concepts.label: Pick-and-place data and throughput
concepts.definition: Placement machines pick parts from feeders and place them at coordinates from the centroid (pick-and-place) file: reference designator, X, Y, rotation and side.

sample.question: A board has 1450 SMT placements. A build of 10 boards runs on a placement machine that sustains 28000 components per hour (CPH) on this job. How many hours of placement time does the build need? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $1450 \cdot 10 / 28000 = 0.52$ hours. Rated CPH is measured on ideal parts; real jobs with large or fine-pitch parts run slower.

concepts.label: Reflow soldering profiles
concepts.definition: Reflow soldering melts printed solder paste in an oven that moves the board through heated zones.

sample.question: A reflow profile is piecewise linear through (0 s, 25 C), (62 s, 150 C), (129 s, 194 C), (173 s, 238 C peak), (216 s, 206 C) and (273 s, 100 C). What is the preheat ramp rate from 25 C to 150 C, in C per second? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $(150 - 25)/62 = 2.02$ C per second. Ramps much above a few C per second risk thermal shock to ceramic capacitors.

concepts.label: Board design rule checking
concepts.definition: Board DRC checks the layout against the fabricator's geometric rules and the design's electrical constraints: clearance between copper on different nets, trace widths, annular rings, drill sizes, hole-to-hole spacing, mask slivers, courtyard overlaps, plus connectivity against the netlist.

sample.question: Board DRC measures clearance between copper shapes as the shortest edge-to-edge distance. A pad on net A covers the rectangle (19, 18) to (43, 36) and a trace segment on net B covers (48, 23) to (65, 36), in mil. What is their clearance, in mil? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: The x gap is 5 mil and the y gap is 0 mil. The shapes overlap in one axis, so the clearance is the other gap, 5 mil.

concepts.label: Design for test on boards
concepts.definition: A built board must be tested for assembly defects: opens, shorts, missing or wrong parts.
key_ideas: The JTAG chain and instruction registers

sample.question: A board has 1140 nets. 537 nets have a probe-able test point for in-circuit or flying-probe test, and 338 other nets have no test point but are reachable through boundary-scan cells. What percentage of nets has some test access? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: $(537 + 338)/1140 = 76.8\%$. Boundary scan recovers access to nets under BGAs that no probe can reach.

concepts.label: Board bring-up and hardware debugging
concepts.definition: Bring-up is the first power-on and functional test of a new board, where design errors that every check missed finally appear.
terms: resistance from each rail to ground

sample.question:
Before a new board is powered for the first time, what should be measured?

A) The clock frequency

B) The trace impedance of every net

C) The resistance from each supply rail to ground, to catch shorts

D) The firmware checksum
sample.answer: The resistance from each supply rail to ground, to catch shorts
sample.explanation: A rail-to-ground short from a solder bridge or a rotated part is common on first articles and is cheap to find unpowered.

concepts.label: Gerber and ODB++
concepts.definition: Fabrication data leaves the board tool in one of a few formats. Gerber (RS-274X, and its attribute-carrying extension X2) describes each layer as a 2D vector image, with drill data in separate Excellon files.

sample.question:
In an RS-274X Gerber file, what does a D03 operation do?

A) Draws a line from the current point with the current aperture

B) Moves the current point without drawing

C) Ends the file

D) Flashes the current aperture at the coordinate, creating a pad image
sample.answer: Flashes the current aperture at the coordinate, creating a pad image
sample.explanation: D01 draws (interpolates), D02 moves, D03 flashes. Pads are usually flashes, traces draws.

concepts.label: IPC standards for design, fabrication and assembly
concepts.definition: IPC standards are the shared vocabulary of the board industry: design rules, land patterns, current capacity, acceptance criteria for bare boards and assemblies, soldering requirements, and data formats.

sample.question:
Which IPC standard gives visual acceptance criteria for electronic assemblies, such as solder fillets?

A) IPC-A-610

B) IPC-2581

C) IPC-2152

D) IPC-A-600
sample.answer: IPC-A-610
sample.explanation: IPC-A-610 is the assembly acceptability standard used by inspectors.

concepts.label: Agents for board constraint setup and placement
concepts.definition: A large share of board-design effort goes into setting up constraints (net classes, matching groups, impedance targets, keep-outs) from datasheets and design guides, and into interactive placement.
key_ideas: The four layers of a board placer

sample.question:
In a board placer built on the four-layer engine model, what belongs in the immutable core?

A) The weight between ratsnest length and thermal spreading

B) Courtyard non-overlap, keep-out and board-outline legality

C) A rule that keeps decoupling capacitors within 2 mm of power pins

D) A hook that streams live congestion maps to an agent
sample.answer: Courtyard non-overlap, keep-out and board-outline legality
sample.explanation: Legality is the invariant every placement must satisfy. Objectives, rules and hooks vary per design and sit above it.

concepts.label: Judging an AI autorouter by DRC and SI
concepts.definition: Learned and agentic autorouters are judged the same way as any engine change: by deterministic checks against golden references.

sample.question: An AI autorouter produced candidate routings of one board. A candidate is accepted only with zero DRC violations and worst intra-pair skew at most 3 ps. The results are: R1: 1 DRC violation, worst intra-pair skew 2 ps; R2: 0 DRC violations, worst intra-pair skew 6 ps; R3: 3 DRC violations, worst intra-pair skew 5.5 ps; R4: 0 DRC violations, worst intra-pair skew 1.5 ps; R5: 0 DRC violations, worst intra-pair skew 3 ps. How many candidates are accepted?
sample.explanation: Apply every gate to every candidate; failing any one rejects it. Accepted: R4, R5. The checks are deterministic tools, so the router cannot talk its way past them.

concepts.label: Schematic-review agents
concepts.definition: Design review of schematics is skilled, tedious work: checking every power pin's decoupling, every regulator's capacitors against its datasheet, every bus's pull-ups, every level crossing between voltage domains.
key_ideas: What the agent checks and from what

sample.question:
Which schematic check is best left to a deterministic rule engine rather than the language model in a review agent?

A) Whether a block's comments describe it well

B) Whether a filter's design intent matches the vendor's application note

C) Whether every input has a driver and every power input has a source (ERC)

D) Whether an alternative part would be cheaper
sample.answer: Whether every input has a driver and every power input has a source (ERC)
sample.explanation: Connectivity rules are exact and cheap to compute. The model's value is in the judgment calls the rules cannot express.

concepts.label: Tool-grounded rewards for board routing
concepts.definition: Training a routing policy with reinforcement learning needs a reward computed by tools: DRC counts, via counts, wirelength against a baseline, skew from the constraint reporter.

sample.question: A routing agent is trained with the tool-grounded reward $R = 100 - 20 V - 0.1 N - 2 W - 5 S$, where $V$ is the DRC violation count, $N$ the via count, $W$ the wirelength excess over the baseline in percent, and $S$ the worst intra-pair skew in ps. Candidate A has 0 DRC violations, 172 vias, 6.5% wirelength excess and 2.5 ps worst skew. What is its reward? Round to 1 decimal place.

concepts.label: PCB and package co-design agents
concepts.definition: The die, its package and the board are designed by different teams in different tools, yet one decision couples them all: which signal sits on which ball.

sample.question:
Which data must stay consistent across the die, package and board databases?

A) The Gerber aperture tables

B) Net names and the mapping from die bumps to package balls to board pads

C) The BOM quantities

D) The silkscreen fonts
sample.answer: Net names and the mapping from die bumps to package balls to board pads
sample.explanation: The three databases describe one connected system. A mismatch in the mapping is an open or short across the boundary.

domains.name: Packaging, Chiplets and 3D Integration
domains.description: Flip chip and BGA, interposers, TSVs, hybrid bonding, UCIe, thermal, mechanical and reliability physics.
covers: Electronic and IC packaging: wire bonding, flip chip, BGA, package substrates, organic and glass substrates
Wafer-level packaging, fan-out WLP, redistribution layers
System in package, multi-chip modules, chiplets, heterogeneous integration, 2.5D integration, interposers, silicon interposers, 3D ICs, TSVs, microbumps, hybrid bonding
Die-to-die interconnect, UCIe, advanced packaging, package-board co-design
Thermal: heat transfer, conduction, thermal resistance, thermal simulation, self-heating, Joule heating, power density, hot spots, thermal management
Mechanical: thermomechanical stress, CTE mismatch, package warpage, FEA
Reliability: electromigration, stress migration, interconnect reliability, dielectric breakdown, aging; multiphysics simulation; thermal-electrical co-design

concepts.label: What a package does
concepts.definition: A package is the structure between a bare die and a printed circuit board. It carries signals and power from the die's fine on-chip pitch out to the board's coarse pitch, removes the die's heat, protects the die mechanically and chemically, and lets the die be tested and handled.
key_ideas: What the package feeds back into design

sample.question:
A team thins a package substrate to shorten its vias for signal integrity. Which package job is most likely to suffer as a side effect?

A) Mechanical: the thinner, less stiff substrate warps more under CTE mismatch

B) Environmental: thin substrates absorb no moisture

C) Thermal: substrates carry most of the heat to the sink

D) Electrical: thinner vias always add inductance
sample.answer: Mechanical: the thinner, less stiff substrate warps more under CTE mismatch
sample.explanation: Stiffness falls steeply with thickness, so the same CTE mismatch bends a thin substrate more. Package jobs are coupled, and a change aimed at one moves another.

concepts.label: Wire bonding
concepts.definition: Wire bonding connects die pads to package leads with thin gold, copper or aluminium wires, bonded by heat, force and ultrasonic energy.

sample.question: A square die of side 7 mm has wire-bond pads in two staggered rows along every edge, each row at a pad pitch of 65 um. Each row holds $\lfloor$side/pitch$\rfloor$ pads per side. How many pads does the die hold in total?
sample.explanation: Per side and row: $\lfloor 7000/65 \rfloor = 107$. Total: $4 \times 2 \times 107 = 856$ pads. Pad count grows with perimeter, not area.

concepts.label: Flip chip and BGA packages
concepts.definition: In flip chip the die is turned face down and joined to the package by solder bumps spread over its whole area.

sample.question: A flip-chip die is 8.5 mm by 17 mm. Bumps sit on a full square grid at 180 um pitch, the first bump half a pitch in from each edge. How many bumps does the die carry?
sample.explanation: $\lfloor 8500/180 \rfloor \times \lfloor 17000/180 \rfloor = 47 \times 94 = 4418$ bumps.

concepts.label: Package substrates: organic and glass
concepts.definition: A package substrate is the small wiring board under the die. Most are organic: a glass-fibre core with build-up dielectric layers and copper traces, made by semi-additive plating.
key_ideas: Layers needed for a signal count

sample.question: A package substrate routes at 15 um line and 6 um space. How many traces can cross a 9 mm die edge using 7 signal layers?
sample.explanation: Per millimetre per layer: $\lfloor 1000/21 \rfloor = 47$. Total: $9 \times 7 \times 47 = 2961$.

concepts.label: BGA escape routing
concepts.definition: Escape routing is the problem of bringing every signal out from inside a dense ball or bump array to the array's edge, so it can be routed onward.
key_ideas: Rows per layer and layer count
Balls escaped on the first layer

sample.question: A BGA has 800 um ball pitch and 320 um pads. The board routes at 60 um trace width and 75 um space. How many traces fit through one channel between adjacent pads, if $n$ traces need $n$ widths and $n+1$ spaces?

concepts.label: Wafer-level and fan-out packaging
concepts.definition: Wafer-level packaging builds the package on the wafer itself, before or instead of dicing into a separate substrate.

sample.question: A fan-in wafer-level package places balls on a full grid under a 7.2 mm by 4.3 mm die at 0.35 mm pitch. How many balls fit, counting $\lfloor$side/pitch$\rfloor$ per side?
sample.explanation: $\lfloor 7.2/0.35 \rfloor \times \lfloor 4.3/0.35 \rfloor = 20 \times 12 = 240$ balls.

concepts.label: Redistribution layers
concepts.definition: A redistribution layer is a thin copper wiring level, insulated by polymer or inorganic dielectric, that moves connections from where the die's pads are to where the bumps or balls must be.
key_ideas: IR drop on RDL power routes

sample.question: An RDL copper trace is 6300 um long, 2 um wide and 2 um thick, with resistivity 2.4 micro-ohm cm. What is its resistance, in ohms? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: 2.4 micro-ohm cm is 0.024 ohm um. $R = 0.024 \times 6300/(2 \times 2) = 37.8$ ohm.

concepts.label: System in package and multi-chip modules
concepts.definition: A system in package (SiP) places several dies, often from different processes, and passive components in one package.

sample.question: A multi-chip module holds 3 untested dies with yields 0.99, 0.92, 0.93. Each die attach succeeds with probability 0.995, independently. What is the module yield, as a percentage? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $Y = 0.995^{3} \times 0.99 \times 0.92 \times 0.93 = 83.44\%$. Every part must be good, so yields multiply.

concepts.label: 2.5D integration on interposers
concepts.definition: In 2.5D integration several dies sit side by side on an interposer, a thin slab carrying fine wiring between them, which in turn sits on a package substrate.

sample.question: A silicon interposer carries 3 dies of 29.5 mm by 10 mm in a row, 0.2 mm apart, with a 0.5 mm margin on every side. A reticle field is 26 mm by 33 mm. Counting by area alone, at least how many reticle fields must be stitched?
sample.explanation: Width $3 \times 29.5 + 2 \times 0.2 + 2 \times 0.5 = 89.9$ mm, height 11 mm, area 988.9 mm^2. $\lceil 988.9/858 \rceil = 2$.

concepts.label: Embedded silicon bridges
concepts.definition: An embedded silicon bridge is a small piece of silicon with fine wiring, placed only under the facing edges of two dies, inside an organic substrate or a mold layer.

sample.question: A full silicon interposer for a multi-die package would be 1200 mm^2. Instead, 6 embedded bridges of 7.5 mm by 2.5 mm connect the facing die edges. By what factor does the silicon area fall? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: Bridge silicon: $6 \times 7.5 \times 2.5 = 112.5$ mm^2. Factor $1200/112.5 = 10.7$.

concepts.label: 3D ICs and TSVs
concepts.definition: A 3D IC stacks dies vertically and connects them through the silicon with through-silicon vias (TSVs): copper-filled holes insulated by an oxide liner.

sample.question: A TSV process fills holes reliably up to an aspect ratio (depth over diameter) of 12. For 4 um diameter TSVs, what is the thickest die, in micrometres, that the TSVs can pass through? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: $t = AR \times d = 12 \times 4 = 48$ um.

concepts.label: TSV keep-out zones
concepts.definition: Copper expands about six times more than silicon per kelvin, so after the anneal and cool-down a TSV leaves residual stress in the silicon around it.
key_ideas: Sizing the keep-out from stress decay

sample.question: A placer blocks a square keep-out around each TSV. The TSV is 5 um in diameter and the keep-out extends 3 um beyond the TSV edge on every side. What area does one TSV block, in square micrometres? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: Side $5 + 2 \times 3 = 11$ um; area $11^2 = 121$ um^2.

concepts.label: TSV capacitance and delay
concepts.definition: A TSV is a copper cylinder inside an oxide liner inside silicon, which makes it a coaxial capacitor to the substrate.
key_ideas: Liner thickness as a design lever

sample.question: A TSV has a copper core of radius 1 um, an oxide liner 0.15 um thick ($\varepsilon_r = 3.9$) and a length of 85 um. Using the coaxial formula $C = 2\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r L/\ln(r_{out}/r_{in})$ with $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-3}$ fF/um, what is its oxide capacitance, in fF? Round to 1 decimal place.

concepts.label: Microbumps
concepts.definition: Microbumps are small solder-capped copper pillars, at pitches of roughly 25 to 55 um, that join dies to interposers, bridges or other dies.

sample.question: A 40 mm^2 interface region is filled with microbumps on a square grid at 40 um pitch. Using density times area, about how many bumps does it hold? Round to the nearest whole number.
sample.explanation: Density $(1000/40)^2 = 625$ per mm^2, times 40 mm^2 gives 25000.

concepts.label: Hybrid bonding
concepts.definition: Hybrid bonding joins two dies or wafers face to face with no solder: polished dielectric surfaces bond directly, and recessed copper pads expand during an anneal to form metal joints.

sample.question: A hybrid-bonding interface places pads on a square grid at 6 um pitch. How many connections per square millimetre does it offer? Round to the nearest whole number.

concepts.label: Chiplet disaggregation and yield
concepts.definition: Disaggregation splits what would be one large die into several smaller chiplets, joined in a package.
key_ideas: Poisson yield of a large die

sample.question: A 240 mm^2 monolithic die is made in a process with 0.26 killer defects per cm^2, randomly scattered. Using the Poisson model $Y = e^{-AD_0}$, what is its yield, as a percentage? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Die-to-die interface choices
concepts.definition: A die-to-die interface is the circuit and protocol that moves data between chiplets in one package.

sample.question:
Two chiplets on a silicon interposer are 2 mm apart. Which interface style suits them best?

A) An optical transceiver per signal

B) A single shared bus with tri-state drivers

C) A wide parallel interface of many single-ended wires at moderate rates, without equalization

D) A few long-reach SerDes lanes with heavy equalization
sample.answer: A wide parallel interface of many single-ended wires at moderate rates, without equalization
sample.explanation: Short dense interposer wires allow simple, low-energy parallel signalling.

concepts.label: Chiplets and UCIe
concepts.definition: Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) is an open die-to-die interconnect standard.

sample.question: A UCIe standard-package module has 16 data lanes per direction, each at 12 GT/s (one bit per transfer). What is its raw bandwidth per direction, in Gb/s?
sample.explanation: $16 \times 12 = 192$ Gb/s each way, before protocol overhead.

concepts.label: Energy per bit and link power
concepts.definition: Energy per bit is the energy an interface spends to move one bit from one die to another, usually quoted in picojoules per bit.

sample.question: A die-to-die link spends 1.75 pJ per bit and carries 25.5 Tb/s in one direction. What power does it draw, in watts? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: 1 pJ/bit at 1 Tb/s is 1 W. $1.75 \times 25.5$ per direction gives 44.62 W in total.

concepts.label: Package-board co-design
concepts.definition: Package-board co-design treats die, package and board as one system. The ball map, the power delivery path and the high-speed channels cross all three, and a choice made in one level, such as a ball assignment, fixes constraints for the others.

sample.question: A core rail draws 122 A, and each package ball may carry at most 0.9 A. How many supply balls are needed for this rail, not counting the ground return?
sample.explanation: $\lceil 122/0.9 \rceil = 136$ balls, with as many ground balls again.

concepts.label: Heat conduction and Fourier's law
concepts.definition: Heat leaves a chip mainly by conduction through solids: silicon, solder, thermal interface material, lid and heat sink, before convection carries it away.
key_ideas: Sizing a material for a budget

sample.question: A layer of mold compound (k = 0.9 W/(m K)) is 710 um thick and 450 mm^2 in area. What is its one-dimensional thermal resistance $L/(kA)$, in K/W? Round to 4 decimal places.
sample.explanation: With $L$ in um and $A$ in mm^2 the factors of $10^{-6}$ cancel: $710/(0.9 \times 450) = 1.7531$ K/W.

concepts.label: Thermal resistance networks
concepts.definition: A thermal resistance network models a package as resistors between temperature nodes, with power as current and temperature as voltage.

sample.question: All the heat of a 70 W die flows in series through: die 0.35 K/W, TIM1 0.34 K/W, lid 0.12 K/W, TIM2 0.4 K/W. Ambient is 48 °C. What is the junction temperature, in °C? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: Series sum 1.21 K/W; $T_j = 48 + 70 \times 1.21 = 132.7$ °C.

concepts.label: Junction temperature and theta values
concepts.definition: Datasheets summarise package thermal behaviour with theta values: thermal resistances between the junction and a reference such as the ambient air, the case or the board, measured under standard conditions.

sample.question: A part dissipates 4 W with $\theta_{ja} = 7.9$ K/W in 42 °C ambient. What is its junction temperature, in °C? Round to 1 decimal place.

concepts.label: Power density and hot spots
concepts.definition: Power density is power per unit area, and its spatial variation, not the total power, decides the peak temperature on a die.

sample.question: A 90 W die has an area of 290 mm^2. What is its average power density, in W/cm^2? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Joule heating and self-heating
concepts.definition: Joule heating is the power $I^2 R$ dissipated when current flows through resistance.

sample.question: A power bump of 18.5 milliohm carries 490 mA. How much power does it dissipate, in milliwatts? Round to 4 decimal places.

concepts.label: Thermal simulation
concepts.definition: Thermal simulation solves the heat equation over the package and die to find the full temperature field, not just a few node values.

sample.question: In a 1-D finite-difference thermal model, each node joins its two neighbours through 1.5 K/W. An interior node receives 0 W of power. Its neighbours currently hold 46 °C and 88.5 °C. What is the node's new temperature after one Jacobi update, in °C? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Transient thermal response
concepts.definition: Temperature does not respond instantly to power. Every material stores heat, which acts as a thermal capacitance, so a power step produces an exponential rise with a thermal time constant.

sample.question: A silicon die is 13 mm by 8 mm and 425 um thick. Silicon has density 2330 kg/m^3 and specific heat 700 J/(kg K). What is the die's thermal capacitance, in mJ/K? Round to 1 decimal place.

concepts.label: Thermal management: TIMs and heat sinks
concepts.definition: Thermal management is the set of materials and devices that move heat from the package to the environment: thermal interface materials (TIMs), lids and spreaders, heat sinks, fans, heat pipes, vapour chambers and liquid cooling.

sample.question: A thermal interface material with conductivity 6 W/(m K) has a 115 um bond line over 100 mm^2. Ignoring contact resistance, what temperature drop does it cause at 110 W, in kelvin? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Thermomechanical stress from CTE mismatch
concepts.definition: Every package joins materials that expand at different rates with temperature: silicon at about 2.6 ppm/K, copper near 17, organic substrates around 14 to 17, mold compounds from under 10 to over 20, and solder near 20.
key_ideas: Biaxial stress in a constrained film
Temperature swing to a stress limit

sample.question: Silicon nitride (3.2 ppm/K) is bonded to a build-up substrate (14 ppm/K) and cooled 230 K from its stress-free temperature. What mismatch strain must the bond accommodate, in ppm? Round to the nearest whole number.
sample.explanation: $\Delta\alpha\Delta T = 10.8 \times 230 = 2484$ ppm.

concepts.label: CTE mismatch and warpage
concepts.definition: Warpage is the out-of-plane bending of a package, wafer or panel caused by CTE mismatch between layers bonded at an elevated temperature.

sample.question: Two bonded layers of equal thickness and equal modulus, 1.3 mm thick in total, differ in CTE by 15.5 ppm/K and cool 220 K from stress-free. Using $\kappa = 3\Delta\alpha\Delta T/(2h)$, what is the radius of curvature, in metres? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: $\kappa = 3 \times 0.0000155 \times 220/(2 \times 0.0013) = 3.9346$ per m; radius $1/\kappa = 0.25$ m.

concepts.label: Solder joint fatigue
concepts.definition: Solder joints between a die and a substrate, or a package and a board, are sheared every time the temperature cycles, because the two sides expand by different amounts.

sample.question: A solder joint of height 110 um sits 2 mm from the neutral point between parts whose CTEs differ by 13.4 ppm/K. For a 70 K temperature swing with no underfill, what is the joint's shear strain $\Delta\alpha\Delta T \cdot DNP/h$, as a percentage? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: Displacement $0.0000134 \times 70 \times 2000 = 1.876$ um over 110 um gives 1.71%.

concepts.label: Finite element analysis of packages
concepts.definition: Finite element analysis (FEA) solves the equations of elasticity, and often plasticity and creep, over a meshed model of the package.
key_ideas: Validation and use in the flow

sample.question:
A package FEA model must predict corner solder-joint strain. How are thousands of joints usually handled?

A) Joints modelled as rigid links

B) A homogenized joint layer globally, with a detailed submodel of the critical corner joints

C) Every joint meshed finely in the global model

D) Joints ignored entirely
sample.answer: A homogenized joint layer globally, with a detailed submodel of the critical corner joints
sample.explanation: Global-local modelling keeps the full model tractable while resolving the joints that fail first.

concepts.label: Electromigration and Black's equation
concepts.definition: Electromigration is the slow transport of metal atoms by the momentum of conducting electrons.

sample.question: A copper line 1.9 um wide and 0.55 um thick carries 5.5 mA. What is its current density, in MA/cm^2? Round to 3 decimal places.

concepts.label: EM temperature acceleration and Blech length
concepts.definition: Electromigration accelerates strongly with temperature through the Arrhenius factor in Black's equation.

sample.question: Electromigration in copper has an activation energy of 0.95 eV. At fixed current density, by what factor is the median life at 95 °C longer than at a 300 °C stress? Use $k = 8.617 \times 10^{-5}$ eV/K. Round to the nearest whole number.

concepts.label: Stress migration and voiding
concepts.definition: Stress migration, also called stress-induced voiding, moves metal atoms under a gradient of mechanical stress rather than electron current.

sample.question:
A via lands on a narrow line in one layout and on a wide plate in another. Which is more vulnerable to stress voiding?

A) Neither, stress voiding needs current

B) Both are equal, since width does not matter

C) The via on the narrow line, because current density is higher

D) The via on the wide plate, because the plate supplies many vacancies
sample.answer: The via on the wide plate, because the plate supplies many vacancies
sample.explanation: Vacancy supply scales with the metal volume feeding the via, which is the reverse of electromigration intuition.

concepts.label: Time-dependent dielectric breakdown
concepts.definition: Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) is the gradual degradation of an insulator under an electric field until a conductive path forms and it shorts.

sample.question: A dielectric 19 nm thick has 1.25 V across it. What is the electric field, in MV/cm? Round to 3 decimal places.
sample.explanation: 1 V/nm is 10 MV/cm, so $E = 10 \times 1.25/19 = 0.658$ MV/cm.

concepts.label: Aging and lifetime guard bands
concepts.definition: Aging is the slow drift of transistor parameters over a product's life, chiefly threshold voltage shifts from bias temperature instability and hot-carrier injection.

sample.question: BTI shifts a transistor's threshold by 23.5 mV after 100 hours of stress, following $\Delta V_{th} \propto t^n$ with $n = 0.22$. What shift is predicted after 15 years of continuous stress (8760 hours per year), in mV? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Electro-thermal multiphysics coupling
concepts.definition: Electrical, thermal and mechanical behaviour are coupled. Current heats conductors, heat raises resistance, higher resistance changes the heat, and temperature drives both stress and electromigration.

sample.question: A conductor has $R(T) = R_0(1 + \beta(T - T_a))$ with $R_0 = 0.1$ ohm and $\beta = 0.0041$ per K, and $T = T_a + \theta I^2 R(T)$ with $\theta = 62$ K/W and $T_a = 52$ °C. It carries 2.7 A. Starting from $T = T_a$, alternate power and temperature updates. What temperature does the second iteration give, in °C? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Partitioning a design across dies
concepts.definition: A 3D or multi-die design must be partitioned: each cell or block is assigned to a die so that the vertical connections stay within budget while area, power and timing balance.

sample.question: A design is split across two dies. Nets: N1 = {b, d, f, h}; N2 = {f, g, h}; N3 = {a, b, d, g}; N4 = {b, d, e, h}; N5 = {f, g}; N6 = {b, d, g, h}; N7 = {b, h}. Assignment: die 0 holds a, b, c, e, g; die 1 holds d, f, h. Each net with cells on both dies needs a vertical connection. How many nets are cut?
sample.explanation: A net is cut when its cells are not all on one die; counting them gives 7.

concepts.label: Inter-die timing
concepts.definition: A timing path that crosses dies passes through drivers, bumps or TSVs, and receivers, and its launch and capture clocks are distributed by separate clock trees on separate dies.
key_ideas: Setup slack across a die boundary

sample.question: A path launches on die A and captures on die B. Clock period 1450 ps; launch clock latency on die A 350 ps; capture clock latency on die B 380 ps. Data delay: 240 ps of logic on die A, 165 ps for the die crossing, 310 ps of logic on die B. Setup time 45 ps. What is the setup slack, in ps?

concepts.label: Thermal-aware 3D floorplanning
concepts.definition: In a 3D stack, dies far from the heat sink must push their heat through the dies nearer to it, and thinned dies spread heat poorly.

sample.question: Two dies are stacked under a heat sink. The die next to the sink connects to ambient (26 °C) through 0.4 K/W, and the far die connects to the near die through 0.2 K/W. All heat leaves through the sink. The near die dissipates 140 W and the far die 20 W. What is the peak temperature in the stack, in °C? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: Near die $26 + 160 \times 0.4 = 90$ °C; far die adds $20 \times 0.2$ to reach 94 °C.

concepts.label: Multi-die assembly verification
concepts.definition: Single-die DRC and LVS prove one die correct against its own netlist. A multi-die package adds new ways to fail: bumps that do not line up between dies, a die flipped or rotated the wrong way, nets connected to the wrong neighbour pin, or package wiring that does not match the system netlist.

sample.question:
Why must the assembly description itself be checked against design intent?

A) It is only used for documentation

B) It replaces the system netlist

C) It is generated by the foundry

D) The checkers treat it as the source of truth, so an error in it hides real errors
sample.answer: The checkers treat it as the source of truth, so an error in it hides real errors
sample.explanation: If the description is wrong, a check can pass on the wrong assembly.

concepts.label: Multiphysics engines in the four-layer model
concepts.definition: Package and 3D-IC analysis runs on multiphysics engines: thermal solvers, mechanical FEA, power-integrity and electromigration checkers, and the coupling between them.
key_ideas: Core and change surface of a multiphysics engine
Placing a request in a tier

sample.question:
Which item is an observation hook rather than a parameter in a coupled electro-thermal engine?

A) The maximum number of coupling iterations

B) The choice of loose or monolithic coupling

C) The thermal conductivity of silicon

D) The live coupling residual and per-die peak temperature exposed during a run
sample.answer: The live coupling residual and per-die peak temperature exposed during a run
sample.explanation: Hooks let an agent read live state; the others are settings chosen before the run.

concepts.label: Fast thermal surrogates versus accurate solvers
concepts.definition: An agent exploring package and 3D floorplans cannot run a full thermal solve for every candidate.
key_ideas: What a fast thermal engine trades away
When to recurse to the accurate solver

sample.question:
Which nonlinearity do fast thermal models often linearize?

A) The geometry of the die

B) Temperature-dependent conductivity and leakage-power feedback

C) The number of dies

D) Fourier's law itself
sample.answer: Temperature-dependent conductivity and leakage-power feedback
sample.explanation: Both make the problem nonlinear; fast models commonly freeze them at a nominal point.

concepts.label: Chiplet partitioning agents and their rewards
concepts.definition: A chiplet partitioning agent proposes how to split a system into dies, which process each die uses, and how they connect, then scores the result with tools: cost and yield models, a partitioner for cut size, die-to-die bandwidth and energy models, and thermal checks.

sample.question:
A partition exceeds the reticle limit for one chiplet. How should the reward treat it?

A) Reject the candidate as infeasible rather than subtracting a small penalty

B) Ignore it until signoff

C) Reward it for using more area

D) Subtract a small penalty and keep it
sample.answer: Reject the candidate as infeasible rather than subtracting a small penalty
sample.explanation: Soft penalties for hard constraints teach the agent to trade violations for gains.

concepts.label: Golden multiphysics checks
concepts.definition: Before an agent's change to a multiphysics engine or flow is accepted, it must pass golden and differential tests.

sample.question:
Which case makes a good golden test for a new 3-D thermal solver?

A) A customer package with no reference result

B) The solver's own previous output on any design

C) A 1-D slab with fixed face temperatures, whose resistance is L/(kA)

D) A random power map with no known answer
sample.answer: A 1-D slab with fixed face temperatures, whose resistance is L/(kA)
sample.explanation: Golden tests need an exact, independent answer.

concepts.label: Agentic package co-design loops
concepts.definition: An agentic package co-design loop reads the reports of package, board, thermal and power-integrity tools, proposes changes such as ball reassignments, decap placement, die order or TIM choice, runs them through the engines and iterates until signoff passes, with a human approving the final change.
key_ideas: What the loop reads and proposes

sample.question:
How should the loop express a proposed ball reassignment?

A) As a typed edit to the design database, validated before any engine runs

B) As a paragraph describing the change

C) As a new RTL module

D) As a hand-edited GDS file
sample.answer: As a typed edit to the design database, validated before any engine runs
sample.explanation: Typed edits are checkable and reviewable.

domains.name: Building EDA Software
domains.description: Design databases, format parsers, incremental computation, deterministic parallelism, regression and QoR, and the open-source RTL-to-GDS flow hands-on.
covers: EDA software architecture: design databases (OpenDB, OpenAccess), object models, hierarchy and instancing
Parsing industry formats: Verilog netlists, Liberty, LEF/DEF, SDC, SPEF, GDS; EDIF, IP-XACT, UPF; Si2 standards
Tcl and Python APIs, domain-specific languages, plug-in architectures, APIs
Incremental computation and dependency graphs (incremental STA, incremental legalization), memory management, cache locality, serialization
Parallel algorithms, concurrency, determinism and reproducible builds, distributed task scheduling, workflow orchestration, cloud computing, containers, Linux
Software engineering for tools: version control, regression testing, continuous integration, QoR tracking, build systems, C++ and Rust in EDA

Open-source EDA hands-on: Yosys, ABC, OpenROAD (OpenDB, OpenSTA, RePlAce, TritonRoute, OpenRCX), OpenROAD-flow-scripts and its GCD design, OpenLane 2, OpenTimer, KLayout, Magic, Netgen, ngspice, Xyce, Xschem, Verilator, cocotb, SymbiYosys
Open PDKs: SKY130, GF180MCU, SG13G2; open-source hardware; what open access does not give you (production readiness, fab access)
License management, commercial tool economics

concepts.label: Design databases
concepts.definition: A design database is the in-memory model that every engine of a physical design tool reads and edits: placement, routing, timing, extraction and verification all work on the same objects.
key_ideas: What the database stores and links

sample.question:
A placer, a router and a timer each read the design from files written by the previous tool. What is the main cost a shared in-memory design database removes?

A) The need for a netlist at all

B) The cost of timing analysis itself

C) The need for technology data such as layers

D) Re-parsing and rebuilding the design between every step
sample.answer: Re-parsing and rebuilding the design between every step
sample.explanation: With file handoff every tool parses LEF, DEF, Verilog and Liberty again and builds its own model. A shared database is built once and every engine reads and edits the same objects.

concepts.label: Blocks, instances, nets and terminals
concepts.definition: Every netlist database names the same handful of objects: a block (the design), instances of master cells, nets, and terminals where nets meet pins.

sample.question: A block holds 23 instances of BUF_X2 (2 signal pins), 7 instances of NOR2_X1 (3 signal pins) and 39 instances of OAI22_X1 (5 signal pins), and the block itself has 4 ports. In an OpenDB-style object model, every signal pin of every instance is one instance terminal (ITerm) and every block port is one block terminal (BTerm). How many ITerms does the block hold?
sample.explanation: An ITerm is the pairing of one instance with one master pin, so the count is the sum of instances times pins: 23 x 2 + 7 x 3 + 39 x 5 = 262. The 4 ports are BTerms, a different object kind.

concepts.label: Hierarchy and instancing
concepts.definition: Designs are written hierarchically: a top module instantiates cores, which instantiate ALUs, which hold leaf cells.

sample.question: Module top holds 56 leaf cells, 7 instances of module core and 3 instances of module periph. Module core holds 120 leaf cells and 6 instances of module alu. Module alu holds 770 leaf cells. Module periph holds 420 leaf cells. How many leaf-cell instances does the flattened design contain?
sample.explanation: Flatten bottom up: one core contains 120 + 6 x 770 = 4740 leaves. Top contains 56 + 7 x 4740 + 3 x 420 = 34496 leaves.

concepts.label: OpenDB
concepts.definition: OpenDB is the design database at the center of OpenROAD. It descends from the Athena database and its schema follows LEF and DEF: technology layers and vias, library masters and pins, and a block of instances, nets, terminals, rows and wires.

sample.question:
In OpenDB, what object represents one instance's connection point for one pin of its master?

A) dbMTerm

B) dbBTerm

C) dbITerm

D) dbNet
sample.answer: dbITerm
sample.explanation: A dbMTerm is a pin of the master cell, a dbBTerm is a port of the block, and a dbITerm is the instance-specific terminal that a dbNet connects to.

concepts.label: Memory footprint of a netlist
concepts.definition: A modern block can have tens of millions of instances and over a hundred million terminals, so bytes per object decide whether a design fits in memory and how fast engines sweep it.

sample.question: A netlist database stores each instance in 80 bytes, each net in 80 bytes and each ITerm in 24 bytes. The design has 200000 instances with an average of 3.8 ITerms each, and 200000 nets. How much memory do these objects take, in megabytes (1 MB = 10^6 bytes)? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: Instances: 200000 x 80 = 16000000 bytes. Nets: 200000 x 80 = 16000000 bytes. ITerms: 760000 x 24 = 18240000 bytes. Total 50240000 bytes, which is 50.2 MB.

concepts.label: Cache locality and data-oriented layouts
concepts.definition: Placement, timing and routing engines spend most of their time in loops over millions of objects, and those loops are usually limited by memory traffic rather than arithmetic.
key_ideas: Cache lines touched by a loop

sample.question: A placer stores 12288 cells as an array of 120-byte structs (array of structures). Its inner loop reads only the 8-byte x coordinate of every cell, in order. Cache lines are 64 bytes and the array starts on a line boundary. How many distinct cache lines does one pass of the loop touch?
sample.explanation: The structs are contiguous, so the loop sweeps the whole array: 12288 x 120 = 1474560 bytes, which is 23040 lines of 64 bytes. Only 8 of every 120 bytes loaded are used.

concepts.label: Handles, arenas and memory management
concepts.definition: An EDA database creates and deletes millions of small objects while several engines hold references to them.

sample.question:
A table reuses the slot of a deleted object. A stale handle to the old object now points at a new one. What prevents the confusion?

A) A mutex around every read

B) A generation counter stored in the handle and the slot

C) Larger indices

D) Sorting the table
sample.answer: A generation counter stored in the handle and the slot
sample.explanation: Each slot increments its generation on reuse. A handle carries the generation it was issued with, so a mismatch reveals a stale reference.

concepts.label: Serializing a design database
concepts.definition: A tool must save its database between flow stages, ship it between machines and reload it quickly.

sample.question: A database writer stores unsigned integers as variable-length integers: 7 payload bits per byte, with the top bit of each byte marking that another byte follows. How many bytes does it write for the values 150408798, 1799956, 2085647, 1048194, 85?
sample.explanation: A value below 2^7 = 128 takes 1 byte, below 2^14 = 16384 takes 2, below 2^21 = 2097152 takes 3, below 2^28 takes 4. Here 150408798 takes 4, 1799956 takes 3, 2085647 takes 3, 1048194 takes 3, 85 takes 1, for 14 bytes.

concepts.label: Tcl evaluation and substitution
concepts.definition: Most EDA tools, OpenROAD and OpenSTA included, are driven by Tcl, and SDC constraint files are Tcl programs.

sample.question: In Tcl, which value does the command `llength {rst {} {u1 a b} clk}` return?
sample.explanation: llength counts top-level elements. A braced group, however much it contains and even when empty, is one element, so the list {rst {} {u1 a b} clk} has 4 elements.

concepts.label: Tcl and Python tool APIs
concepts.definition: EDA engines are written in C++ for speed, but users and flows drive them from scripts.
key_ideas: What to script and what to compile

sample.question:
Besides Tcl, what scripting interface does OpenROAD offer for working with its database and engines?

A) A JavaScript interface running in a browser

B) No other interface; Tcl is the only way in

C) A Python interface to the same engines and database objects

D) A Perl interface only for reports
sample.answer: A Python interface to the same engines and database objects
sample.explanation: OpenROAD can run with a Python interpreter, giving access to the database objects and engine calls, which suits data analysis and machine-learning work.

concepts.label: Domain-specific languages for EDA
concepts.definition: EDA is full of small languages: SDC for constraints, Liberty for cell libraries, UPF for power intent, rule decks for DRC and LVS, synthesis scripts, and flow configuration files.

sample.question:
Liberty has its own grammar of groups and attributes and no loops or variables. What kind of language is it?

A) An external declarative data language

B) An embedded scripting language

C) A general-purpose programming language

D) A hardware description language
sample.answer: An external declarative data language
sample.explanation: Liberty is declarative data with a dedicated parser. It describes cells; it does not compute.

concepts.label: Parsing structural Verilog netlists
concepts.definition: After synthesis, a design travels as a structural Verilog netlist: a module with ports, wire declarations and instances of library cells.
key_ideas: Instances, nets and terminals in the text
Positional connections need the cell's port order

sample.question: A parser reads this netlist into a design database: `module top (a, b, c, y0, y1); input a, b, c; output y0, y1; wire n1, n2; NOR2_X1 u1 (.A1(a), .A2(a), .ZN(n1)); AOI21_X1 u2 (.A(c), .B1(c), .B2(n1), .ZN(y0)); BUF_X1 u3 (.A(b), .Z(n2)); AOI21_X1 u4 (.A(b), .B1(n2), .B2(n1), .ZN(y1)); endmodule` How many instance terminals (ITerms) does it create? Count one per pin of every instance, inputs and outputs.
sample.explanation: One ITerm per instance pin: u1 has 3, u2 has 4, u3 has 2, u4 has 4, for 13 in all. Ports become BTerms, not ITerms.

concepts.label: Parsing Liberty
concepts.definition: Liberty (.lib) files carry the timing, power and function of every library cell, and every synthesis, timing and power tool must read them.
key_ideas: What the parser must keep for timing

sample.question:
Why can one grammar parse every Liberty file even though vendors add their own attributes?

A) Unknown attributes are rejected, so files only use standard names

B) Vendors must register each attribute with the parser at build time

C) The grammar lists every legal attribute name explicitly

D) Every statement is a group, a simple attribute or a complex attribute, whatever its name
sample.answer: Every statement is a group, a simple attribute or a complex attribute, whatever its name
sample.explanation: The syntax does not depend on the attribute vocabulary. A parser can keep or skip unknown names and still recover the structure.

concepts.label: Liberty units and scaling
concepts.definition: Liberty tables are just numbers; their meaning comes from unit attributes in the library header.
key_ideas: Capacitive load units scale pins and indices

sample.question: A Liberty library header declares `time_unit : "1ps" ;`. A cell_rise table entry for one arc reads 161.1. What is that delay in ps? Round to 1 decimal place.
sample.explanation: Table values are in the library time unit, 1ps = 1 ps, so 161.1 × 1 = 161.1 ps.

concepts.label: Parsing LEF and DEF
concepts.definition: LEF and DEF are the physical interchange formats of digital implementation. LEF describes the technology and the abstract of each cell; DEF describes one design's floorplan, instances, pins, nets and routing.
key_ideas: DEF sections and what they build

sample.question:
Which LEF content does a placer need to put a standard cell into a row?

A) The MACRO's SIZE, its SITE and its CLASS

B) The VIA definitions

C) The routing layer PITCH values

D) The MACRO's PIN shapes on metal1 only
sample.answer: The MACRO's SIZE, its SITE and its CLASS
sample.explanation: SIZE gives the footprint, SITE says which rows it fits, and CLASS separates core cells from pads and blocks.

concepts.label: DEF database units
concepts.definition: DEF stores every coordinate as an integer in database units, declared once by `UNITS DISTANCE MICRONS n`.

sample.question: A DEF file declares `UNITS DISTANCE MICRONS 100 ;` and its COMPONENTS section has `- u9422 NOR2_X1 + PLACED ( 87625 32547 ) N ;`. What is the x coordinate of the instance origin in microns? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: DEF stores integers in database units; one micron is 100 units, so 87625 / 100 = 876.25 microns.

concepts.label: SDC as Tcl
concepts.definition: SDC is the language of timing intent: clocks, input and output delays, exceptions.

sample.question:
An SDC line reads `set_input_delay 0.4 -clock clk {in_a in_b}`. What do the braces do?

A) Run a command named in_a

B) Evaluate in_a and in_b as variables

C) Pass the two names as one list word, without substitution

D) Mark the names as optional
sample.answer: Pass the two names as one list word, without substitution
sample.explanation: Braces quote a word literally; the result is a Tcl list, which the command reads as two port names.

concepts.label: Parsing SPEF
concepts.definition: SPEF (Standard Parasitic Exchange Format) carries the resistances and capacitances extracted from routed wires, net by net.

sample.question: A SPEF writer can replace the net name u_cpu/u_alu/n_35681 (19 characters) by the index *35538 through *NAME_MAP. The name appears 11 times in the file. Each name-map line is the index, a space, the name and a newline. How many bytes does the map save?
sample.explanation: Without the map the name costs 11 × 19 = 209 bytes. With it, references cost 11 × 6 = 66 and the map line costs 6 + 1 + 19 + 1 = 27, so the saving is 116 bytes.

concepts.label: GDSII stream records
concepts.definition: GDSII is the binary stream format in which layouts reach the mask shop, and KLayout, Magic and every DRC engine read and write it.
key_ideas: Record headers and the XY record

sample.question: A GDSII writer emits a BOUNDARY for a rectangle with 4 distinct vertices. Every record starts with a 4-byte header (2-byte length that includes the header, 1-byte record type, 1-byte data type), each coordinate is a 4-byte signed integer, and a boundary repeats its first point to close. How many bytes long is the XY record?
sample.explanation: The closed boundary stores 4 + 1 = 5 points, each an (x, y) pair of 8 bytes, plus the 4-byte header: 4 + 8 × 5 = 44 bytes.

concepts.label: EDIF, IP-XACT, UPF and Si2 standards
concepts.definition: Beyond Verilog, Liberty, LEF/DEF, SPEF and GDS, a tool meets a set of interchange standards for netlists, IP metadata and power intent.
key_ideas: UPF power intent and the Si2 coalitions

sample.question:
An FPGA vendor tool exports a netlist with nested parenthesized forms such as `(cell ... (view ... (interface ...) (contents ...)))`. Which format is it?

A) EDIF

B) SPEF

C) IP-XACT

D) UPF
sample.answer: EDIF
sample.explanation: EDIF uses LISP-like S-expressions to describe libraries, cells, views, interfaces and contents.

concepts.label: One database, many engines
concepts.definition: An EDA flow chains engines: floorplanner, placer, clock-tree builder, router, extractor, timer.

sample.question:
Point tools from different vendors exchange LEF, DEF, Verilog and SPEF. What does that architecture get right?

A) It lets tools share memory directly

B) Any tool can be swapped, because the formats are the contract between them

C) It removes all parsing work

D) It guarantees the same results from every vendor
sample.answer: Any tool can be swapped, because the formats are the contract between them
sample.explanation: Standard formats decouple tools. The cost is the serialization at every boundary.

concepts.label: Plug-in architectures
concepts.definition: Every long-lived EDA tool grows by extension: new synthesis passes, new placement penalties, new reports, new readers.

sample.question:
What does a plug-in registry store per entry?

A) The plug-in's source code

B) A copy of the design database

C) A name and a way to construct the implementation (a factory)

D) The plug-in's test results
sample.answer: A name and a way to construct the implementation (a factory)
sample.explanation: The registry maps names to constructors; the host creates instances on demand.

concepts.label: Database callbacks and observers
concepts.definition: When engines share one design database, an engine that caches derived data, a timer's arrival times or a placer's density map, must learn when the design changes.

sample.question: A design database notifies registered observers on every edit: the power analyzer subscribes to master swapped and pin connected or disconnected; the density map subscribes to pin connected or disconnected and instance created; the timer subscribes to instance created; the parasitic estimator subscribes to master swapped and instance created. An optimizer then makes these edits in order: master swapped, master swapped, instance created, instance moved, instance moved. How many callback invocations does the database make in total?
sample.explanation: Each edit calls every observer subscribed to its kind: 2 + 2 + 3 + 0 + 0, which sums to 7.

concepts.label: Incremental computation and dependency graphs
concepts.definition: Every EDA tool caches derived results: parasitics computed from wires, delays from parasitics, arrivals from delays, slacks from arrivals.
key_ideas: A query needs only its dirty ancestors

sample.question: A tool caches derived results in a dependency graph whose edges run from an input to a result computed from it: D→K, A→F, G→D, A→E, F→C, F→G. An edit directly modifies F. How many results, not counting the edited node itself, must be marked invalid?
sample.explanation: Invalidation follows edges forward: every result reachable from F may now be stale. Those are C, D, G, K, 4 results.

concepts.label: Dirty flags and lazy invalidation
concepts.definition: A dirty flag is one bit per cached result that says "my inputs changed since I was computed." Setting flags is cheap, recomputing is not, and the gap between the two is where incremental tools win.

sample.question: A dependency graph has edges from input to derived result: H→M, L→N, A→H, B→A, B→J, B→L, L→Q, H→N, Q→G, H→J. A script applies 2 edits in sequence, changing Q, then A, and then queries every result once. Assume every downstream result changes. With eager recomputation, each edit immediately recomputes every result downstream of the edited node. How many result evaluations happen in total?
sample.explanation: Eager evaluation pays for each edit separately: Q reaches 1, A reaches 4, for 5 evaluations. Results shared by several edits are recomputed each time.

concepts.label: Incremental STA inside a tool
concepts.definition: Inside an optimizer, a static timer is not a batch program that reads files and prints a report.
key_ideas: Edits reach the timer through callbacks
Invalidate, then propagate in level order
What makes an incremental update expensive

sample.question:
An in-process timer keeps its own graph of vertices for pins and edges for arcs. A net is deleted from the database. What must the timer's callback do before anything else touches the graph?

A) Delete every vertex in the net's fanout cone

B) Re-run levelization of the whole graph immediately

C) Remove or detach the wire arcs of that net and mark its former loads invalid

D) Nothing, because nets are not timing objects
sample.answer: Remove or detach the wire arcs of that net and mark its former loads invalid
sample.explanation: The timer's graph must stay consistent with the database. Wire arcs of a deleted net would point at dead objects; the loads now see a different driver and are stale.

concepts.label: Incremental legalization
concepts.definition: After global placement, a legalizer snaps every cell to a row and a site without overlap.
key_ideas: Total displacement and when to stop

sample.question: A placement row holds, left to right, c1 at x = 1 (width 6), c2 at x = 8 (width 5), c3 at x = 14 (width 6), c4 at x = 20 (width 2), c5 at x = 22 (width 6), c6 at x = 28 (width 6), all in site units. A resize ECO widens c1 by 9 sites, keeping its left edge fixed. The incremental legalizer only pushes cells to the right, each by the least amount that removes its overlap, and leaves every other cell alone. How many cells move?
sample.explanation: c1 now ends at 16. Walking right, each cell starts at the larger of its old x and the end of its left neighbour: c2 → 16, c3 → 21, c4 → 27, c5 → 29, c6 → 35. Shifting stops at the first cell whose gap absorbs the push. 5 cells move.

concepts.label: Content-addressed result caching
concepts.definition: Flows recompute the same things over and over: a regression reruns unchanged designs, a parameter sweep shares its synthesis step, a developer reruns placement after editing only a report script.

sample.question: A flow caches the result of an extraction step keyed by a hash of its inputs. A lookup costs 18 s (hashing the inputs and probing the store), and on a miss the step runs for 360 s after the lookup. The hit rate is 61%. What is the expected time per invocation, in seconds? Round to 2 decimal places.
sample.explanation: Every call pays the lookup; only misses pay the computation: 18 + (1 - 0.61) × 360 = 158.4 s.

concepts.label: Amdahl's law and parallel speedup
concepts.definition: EDA runs are long, and machines have many cores, so every engine author is asked how much faster the tool gets with more threads.
key_ideas: The ceiling of one over s
Serial fraction from a target speedup

sample.question: Profiling shows that 27% of a DRC run is serial (reading the database, building data structures, writing results) and the rest parallelizes perfectly. What speedup does the run reach on 64 threads? Round to 2 decimal places.

concepts.label: Thread pools and partitioned work
concepts.definition: Parallel EDA engines rarely spawn a thread per task. They split the work into pieces (regions for routing, nets for extraction, partitions for placement) and feed them to a fixed pool of worker threads.

sample.question: A router splits a design into 7 independent regions whose routing times are 8, 3, 6, 11, 5, 9, 6 ms, and runs them on a pool of 3 worker threads. Tasks are taken in the listed order, and each goes to the worker that becomes free first (the lowest-numbered one on a tie). What is the makespan, in ms?
sample.explanation: Greedy list scheduling gives worker loads 17, 14, 17 ms; the makespan is the largest, 17 ms.

concepts.label: Deterministic parallelism
concepts.definition: A deterministic engine gives bit-identical results for identical inputs, every run.

sample.question:
A placer sums the wirelength gradient over all nets with a parallel reduction. Run twice with the same input and 16 threads, it reports total wirelengths that differ in the 12th digit. What is the cause?

A) A data race corrupted memory in one run

B) Floating-point addition is not associative, and the reduction order differed

C) The random seed is reset differently on each run

D) Double precision is too short to hold a wirelength
sample.answer: Floating-point addition is not associative, and the reduction order differed
